Triggers.value: Visible injuries or wounds on others
Physical pain in a part of the body

Threat.value: I avoid going to unfamiliar places because I cannot assess the danger
I frequently look behind me to check if someone is following me
I always identify escape routes before I feel comfortable anywhere

Negative Appraisals.value: I feel isolated and set apart from others
I am not sure my life is worth living anymore
There is something about me that made the event happen

vignette: Carlos still remembers the sound of shattering glass and the screams that followed. It was a routine traffic stop gone wrong; he had been driving home from a late-night meeting with a client when police officers approached his car, guns drawn. The next thing he knew, he was being dragged out of the vehicle and thrown to the ground. A kick to the ribs left him gasping for air as he watched in horror as one of the officers slammed his head into the pavement. The memories of that night still haunt Carlos. Visible injuries or wounds on others now trigger a wave of anxiety; he can't help but think of his own battered body, the blood streaming down his face, and the feeling of utter powerlessness. Reminders of victims - news reports, conversations with friends who have had similar experiences - bring it all flooding back. Even physical pain in a part of his body, like the lingering ache in his ribs, can transport him back to that night. As he navigates his daily routine as a tax consultant, Carlos finds himself increasingly isolated and set apart from others. He feels like there's something about him that made the event happen - maybe it was his Latin American heritage, or perhaps it was just bad luck. Whatever the reason, he can't shake the feeling that he's to blame. His clients seem oblivious to his struggles, but Carlos is convinced they can see right through him, that they know he's not worth their time. Avoiding unfamiliar places has become second nature for Carlos; he sticks to routes he knows like the back of his hand, always on high alert for potential dangers lurking around every corner. He frequently looks over his shoulder, half-expecting to see a police officer or someone else with malicious intentions following him. Even in his own office, he identifies escape routes before feeling comfortable - just in case. The weight of these constant threat assessments has taken its toll on Carlos's mental health. He's started questioning whether his life is worth living anymore; the isolation and feelings of intrinsic fault have convinced him that he's a burden to those around him. His negative appraisals, in turn, fuel his hypervigilance - if he's not constantly on guard, he's sure something terrible will happen. As Carlos navigates this self-reinforcing cycle, he finds himself increasingly trapped. Triggers like visible injuries or victim memories send him spiraling back into the abyss of negative appraisals and threat assessments. It's a vicious loop that has finally brought him to seek help - not because he hopes to break free from it entirely, but because he fears what might happen if he doesn't. Carlos's eyes scan the therapist's office as he settles onto the couch, his gaze lingering on potential escape routes before returning to the present moment. He takes a deep breath and begins to recount his story, the words spilling out in a rush of anxiety and despair. As he speaks, it becomes clear that this is just the beginning - the first tentative step towards untangling the complex web of triggers, threats, and negative appraisals that has come to define his life.
